reformulations.declaration: Erdos274.herzog_schonheim (the canonical statement this mirror file points to; it lives in the imported module FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/274.lean)
reformulations.difference: Wikipedia (and Margolis–Schnabel's precise statement, arXiv:1803.03569) take a partition {a_1G_1,…,a_kG_k} of a group G into k>1 left cosets of subgroups, which are of finite index, and say the indices cannot be pairwise distinct. The Lean statement differs in four ways. (i) It uses an ι-indexed `Group.ExactCovering`: cosets pairwise disjoint for distinct indices, union = univ. (ii) It has no finite-index hypothesis and uses `Subgroup.index`, which is 0 for infinite index. (iii) It adds the hypothesis `hG : 1 < ENat.card G`. (iv) It concludes `∃ i j, i ≠ j ∧ (P.parts i).index = (P.parts j).index` instead of 'not pairwise distinct'. A reader might flag (ii) as the Mathlib junk-value trap (0 = 0 for two infinite-index parts) or (iii) as an extra restriction.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: (ii) B. H. Neumann's lemma (Mathlib `Subgroup.leftCoset_cover_filter_FiniteIndex`): cosets of infinite-index subgroups can be dropped from a finite coset cover. In an exact covering, dropping the coset of `parts i` would leave `reps i` uncovered, because the cosets are disjoint. So every part has finite index, `Subgroup.index` is the true index, and the value 0 is never reached. (iii) `hG` follows from `1 < Fintype.card ι`: the representatives of two distinct indices lie in disjoint cosets, so they differ. (i) Nonempty, pairwise disjoint cosets indexed by ι are exactly a set partition with |ι| blocks, and a coset gU determines U. So k > 1 ⇔ `1 < Fintype.card ι`, and the indices match. (iv) is De Morgan. The Lean statement covers all groups, as Wikipedia does. The finite case is equivalent anyway: Margolis–Schnabel note it suffices to prove the conjecture for finite groups (Korec–Znám). Proved in /workspace/review/scratch2.lean, axioms only propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound: `finiteIndex : ∀ i, (P.parts i).FiniteIndex` for any `Group.ExactCovering`; `hG_redundant : 1 < Fintype.card ι → 1 < ENat.card G`; and `HSsource ↔ type_of% @Erdos274.herzog_schonheim`. Here HSsource is the source form: an exact covering with 1 < card ι and all parts of finite index, no hG, conclusion ¬(∀ i ≠ j, index i ≠ index j). Non-vacuity was checked in scratch3.lean: the partition of a finite group into singletons is a `Group.ExactCovering`, instantiated for Multiplicative (ZMod 3) with 3 parts.

review.notes:
The file under review is an import-only mirror file. This follows the repository convention for mirror files (the #3608 cleanup removed their duplicate `type_of%` theorems; other Wikipedia mirrors such as HappyEndingProblem and BrocardProblem have the same shape). It contains no declarations, so nothing in it can state a wrong claim. It elaborates cleanly.

What I checked:
- **Module docstring.** Its claim that the canonical formalization is in `FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«274»` is correct: that module contains `Erdos274.herzog_schonheim`.
- **References.** All four are papers about the Herzog–Schönheim conjecture, with correct IDs: Chouraqui IJAC 2019; Margolis–Schnabel; Chouraqui DLT 2020 (the PMC one); Chouraqui arXiv:1804.11103.
- **The pointed-to statement.** `Erdos274.herzog_schonheim` is faithful to Wikipedia's statement; see the reformulation entry, including the Lean proofs.

Status: HS is still open. Wikipedia lists it among unsolved problems, and the teorth erdosproblems data records Erdős 274 (= HS) as open. The target is tagged `research open`, which matches. The PMC paper says "So, the HS conjecture is true for all groups", but that sentence ends the proof of its Theorem 2, which begins "Assume Conjecture 1 is true". It is a conditional result, not a resolution.

Also looked at, outside this file's scope:
- **`Erdos274.erdos_274`** (Erdős' form, "cosets of different sizes", with `#(P.parts i)`). For infinite G, every finite-index subgroup has cardinality #G, so pairwise distinct cardinalities are only possible in finite G. There, distinct cardinalities ⇔ distinct indices. So its right-hand side is equivalent to ¬HS, using the Korec–Znám reduction to finite groups. I did not prove this in Lean. I also could not recheck the exact erdosproblems.com wording because of Cloudflare; that is the 274 file's concern.
- **`erdos_274.variants.abelian`** is HS for finite abelian groups. That case is known: Margolis–Schnabel cite Berger–Felzenbaum–Fraenkel for pyramidal groups, which include abelian groups.
